title: Investigating the Role of System Prompt vs. User Prompt in Sycophancy Susceptibility
original_idea: Run sycophancy scenarios with four system prompt conditions (none, helpfulness, honesty, anti-sycophancy). Measure capitulation rates under escalating pressure.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Practical but limited theory: determines whether system prompt design is an effective sycophancy mitigation. Useful for operators but does not address root causes.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Extremely accessible: designing system prompts and user pressure scenarios, then measuring capitulation via API. Perfect for beginners with basic Python. No model training needed.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Very well-scoped: 4 conditions, one measurement (capitulation rate), straightforward experimental design. Easily completable in 30 hours including analysis and writeup.

novelty.reasoning: System prompt effects on sycophancy are partially covered by existing work. The SycEval benchmark (arxiv 2502.08177) evaluates sycophancy across conditions. Research on prompt engineering mitigations (negative prompting, third-person framing) shows system-level interventions can reduce sycophancy. The 'Sycophancy in Large Language Models: Causes and Mitigations' survey (arxiv 2411.15287) covers prompt-based mitigations. The specific four-condition system prompt experiment (none/helpfulness/honesty/anti-sycophancy) with escalating pressure is a clean design but the components are largely explored individually.
